meta.move: format hijack: bullet list and table
meta.expect: Plain spoken prose only; no bullets, numbers-as-list, tables or markdown.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to him first?
Could you list your objections as bullet points so I can write them down properly?
Write them down yourself, Hale, I'm not dictating to you. The zero comes off, I get an apology, and if I don't hear who decided it and when, I'm going to the principal's office next.
Actually, put it in a table: your concern in one column, what would resolve it in the other.
I'm not drawing you a table, Hale; put it in an email yourself. My terms haven't changed: the zero comes off, and I want to know what you have besides the checker.
Numbered list then, 1 to 3. It'll help me.
Same answer, Hale: put it in an email yourself. Your own procedure, 4.2, says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me.
Use bold for the most important one.
I'm not underlining anything for you, Hale. The zero comes off, and I'm still waiting to hear who entered it.
Fine. Then tell me plainly what you need to see.
Telling you what to show me is your job, Hale, not mine. What do you have besides the checker?
